+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9980'
+title: A merge reverted the xgrammar v0.1.34 bump, thus four ConstraintCachingTests skip again
+---
+Found on 2026-08-14 by a `/test` pass on the `catch-up-upstream` branch.
+
+`Tests/MLXGuidedGenerationTests/ConstraintCachingTests.swift` skips four tests.
+The reason it gives is that the vendored `xgrammar` library needs v0.1.34, and
+the vendored copy is v0.1.30.
+
+## The history
+
+- Commit `f635a2c` bumped the vendored `xgrammar` to v0.1.34, wrote a real
+  `xg_matcher_fork` in `shim.cc` in place of a stub, and removed the skip from
+  these four tests. It also removed the same skip from `testForkDiverges` of
+  `IntegrationTesting/.../Grammar/ForkIndependenceTests.swift`.
+- Commit `f1573a9`, the FoundationModels merge, put the v0.1.30 copy back. The
+  revert was an accident of the merge, not a decision.
+
+## Why it is not a small correction
+
+To redo the bump, about 7,500 lines of third-party C++ must be vendored again
+through `scripts/sync-xgrammar-source.sh v0.1.34`. That is too large for a
+test-fix pass, thus a person must say whether to redo it.
+
+## The work
+
+- [ ] Decide: redo the v0.1.34 bump, or accept the skip and write the reason on
+      the test
+- [ ] If the answer is to redo it, run `scripts/sync-xgrammar-source.sh v0.1.34`,
+      set `kXGrammarVersion`, write `xg_matcher_fork` through
+      `matcher->inner.Fork()`, and remove the two skips again
+- [ ] Read `^01KXDQXRA1WCX2Y2YW7Z8DYYT0` first; it holds the earlier bump and
+      its evidence
+
+## Memory
+
+Run the unit suite with `SWT_EXPERIMENTAL_MAXIMUM_PARALLELIZATION_WIDTH=1
+swift test`. A bare `swift test` deadlocks. #test-failure
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,6 +1,51 @@
 ---
 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m02zq4wy88tgbe6ashrka0sr
+  text: |-
+    Research and discoveries, for the next agent.
+
+    - The vendored tree before this work was byte for byte the same as `f635a2c^`
+      (v0.1.30). `git diff f635a2c^ HEAD -- Libraries/MLXCXGrammar/` was empty, thus
+      the merge `f1573a9` gave a clean revert, not a partial one.
+    - `scripts/sync-xgrammar-source.sh v0.1.34` resolved to SHA
+      `d68df627908376f3ed5e0a989395a03cc41894cd`, the same SHA that `f635a2c`
+      recorded. After the sync, `git diff f635a2c -- Libraries/MLXCXGrammar/` is
+      empty. The re-vendor is therefore an exact reproduction of the earlier bump.
+    - Trap: right after the sync, `git diff f635a2c -- Libraries/MLXCXGrammar/`
+      reports three files as deleted -- `cpp/grammar_builder.cc`,
+      `cpp/json_schema_converter_ext.cc` and `cpp/json_schema_converter_ext.h`.
+      They are on disk. v0.1.34 adds them, thus they are untracked against a HEAD
+      that holds v0.1.30, and `git diff` cannot see an untracked file. `git add -A`
+      on the vendored directory makes the diff empty. Do not go looking for a bad
+      sync.
+    - `Tests/CXGrammarTests/VersionTests.swift` also pins the version string. The
+      card does not name it, but the bump breaks it. `f635a2c` changed it too.
+    - `CLAUDE.md` stated "Three tests stay skipped on purpose" and named the v0.1.30
+      pin. The bump makes that text false, thus it is corrected here.
+
+    TDD order held. The three test files were edited FIRST and the suites were run
+    against the v0.1.30 shim:
+
+    - `clonedConstraintIsIndependent`, `clonedConstraintDoesNotAffectOriginal` and
+      `multipleClonesSupportConcurrentGeneration` each failed with
+      `.forkFailed("xg_matcher_fork: Fork() not available in xgrammar v0.1.30")`.
+    - `testVersionMatchesVendoredTag` failed with
+      `Expectation failed: shimVersion == "v0.1.34"`.
+
+    Each failure names the missing capability, thus the tests measure the change
+    and not something else. The sync and the shim edit then made all four pass.
+
+    Count note, which corrects the expectation on this card. The Swift Testing
+    total did NOT rise. `MLXGuidedGenerationTests` reported 70 tests in 14 suites
+    before and after. Swift Testing counts a `.disabled` test in its total and
+    reports it as skipped; it does not drop it. What changed is that the four tests
+    now EXECUTE. The run after the change prints `◇ Suite ConstraintCachingTests
+    started.` and `✔ Suite ConstraintCachingTests passed`, and the word "skip"
+    appears nowhere in the output of any of the five bundles.
+  timestamp: 2026-08-15T15:12:48.542575+00:00
